components.css: :host{--bg:#0f1115;--surface:#181b21;--surface-2:#20242c;--border:#2b303a;--text:#f3f1ec;--muted:#9aa0ab;--accent:#d97757;--accent-text:#1a0f0a;--danger:#ff6369;--ok:#46a758;--warn:#f5a524;--radius:14px;--shadow:0 8px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif;color:var(--text)} .ds-deck{--key:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.055);--key-edge:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.07);--key-press:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.15);--deck-light:#f5a524;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:0.5rem;padding:0.6rem;border-radius:24px;background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 58%, transparent);backdrop-filter:blur(24px) saturate(160%);border:1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.06),0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--deck-light) 24%, transparent),0 12px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2);max-width:360px} .ds-key{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:0.2rem;height:56px;border:1px solid var(--key-edge);border-radius:14px;background:var(--key);color:var(--text);font:inherit;cursor:pointer;transition:transform 0.08s ease,background-color 0.15s ease} .ds-key:active{transform:scale(0.96);background:var(--key-press)} .ds-key:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px} .ds-cap{font-size:0.72rem;font-weight:600;color:var(--muted)} .ds-accept{--tone:var(--ok)} .ds-reject{--tone:var(--danger)} .ds-lit{background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 20%, var(--key));border-color:color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 55%, transparent)} .ds-lit svg,.ds-lit .ds-cap{color:var(--tone)} .ds-mic{grid-column:span 3;flex-direction:row;gap:0.55rem;background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, var(--key));border-color:color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 32%, transparent)} .ds-mic svg{color:var(--accent)} .ds-mic .ds-cap{font-size:0.85rem;color:var(--text)}

narrative.overview:
VoiceCode is a piece of studio hardware that happens to run in a phone browser. It sits next to the keyboard like a stream deck or a synth controller: a dark, warm body, rounded keys you press with a thumb, and one soft light that tells you what Claude is doing without you having to read anything. The rest of the app (pairing, transcript, settings) is the instrument's quiet manual: flat ink surfaces, system type, generous 44px targets.

Density is medium and deliberate. Every control is finger-sized and reachable with one hand, and text is set at a size that reads at arm's length next to a monitor. Expression is concentrated in exactly two places: the Kiln Terracotta accent that marks what you can act on, and the deck's state light. Everything else holds back so those two stay legible.

It must never read as gamer RGB, a generic SaaS dashboard, a chat-app clone or skeuomorphic chrome. It is a calm instrument, not a toy, a report or a messenger.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ink in dark mode, warm paper in light; both meet WCAG AA.
One accent, Kiln Terracotta, for primary actions, the user's own messages and attention.
Pills for actions, 14px rounded rectangles for keys and cards, a 24px glass slab for the deck.
Flat and tonal everywhere except the deck (frosted glass + state light) and things that interrupt you (approvals, sheets, toasts), which lift with a shadow.
Tactile and calm: presses scale to 0.96–0.97, nothing glows unless it means something.

rules.name: The One Clay Rule
rules.body: Kiln Terracotta is the only brand colour. It marks what you can act on or what needs you; it is never a background for a whole region or a decorative stripe.

rules.name: The Light Means State Rule
rules.body: Cyan, amber, green, red, grey and violet exist to report Claude's state through the deck light and command keys. Never use them for decoration, categories or charts.

rules.name: The Two Red Keys Rule
rules.body: When Reject is lit, Stop colours only its glyph so two red keys never compete.

rules.name: The No Display Face Rule
rules.body: No web fonts and nothing above 2rem. An instrument labels its controls; it doesn't headline them.

rules.name: The Glass Stays on the Deck Rule
rules.body: Frosted glass (`blur(24px) saturate(160%)`) and the blurred state light belong to the deck only. Headers, sheets and cards stay opaque and flat.

rules.name: The Lift Means Interrupt Rule
rules.body: A shadow says "this needs you now": approvals, sheets, toasts. Static content never gets one.

dos: Do keep every interactive target at least 44px tall, and approval actions at 50px.
Do show a tool call's complete input in the mono well of the permission card before Approve is reachable.
Do define new colours in both themes and check WCAG AA in dark and light.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: drop the light's drift and pulses, keep the colour change.
Do give presses a small scale (0.96–0.97) and keep transitions at 0.08–0.25s; only the state light moves slowly (0.6s+).
donts: Don't use rainbow glows, neon saturation or multiple simultaneous light colours (gamer RGB).
Don't add stat-tile grids, gradient hero cards or blue-purple gradients (generic SaaS dashboard).
Don't make the Claude tab look like a chat app; the deck and approvals lead, the transcript supports.
Don't add bevels, fake metal, textures or photographic materials (skeuomorphic chrome).
Don't spread glass or blur beyond the deck, or put shadows on static content.
Don't use state colours for decoration or fill a button with red.
